questions.question: A and B can complete the work in 15 days and 20 days, respectively. They start together, but every 3rd day, B is absent. In how many days will the work be completed?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM(15, 20) = 60 units. Efficiency of A = 4, B = 3.

Work cycle (3 days): Day 1 (A+B) + Day 2 (A+B) + Day 3 (A) = 7 + 7 + 4 = 18 units.

In 3 cycles (9 days): 18 × 3 = 54 units. Remaining work = 60 − 54 = 6 units.

Time for remaining 6 units (Day 10, A+B working): 6 ÷ 7 days.

Total time = 9 + 6/7 = 9(6/7) days.

**∴ The correct answer is 9(6/7) days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

questions.question: A car travels 60 km at x km/h, 90 km at y km/h, 120 km at z km/h. If average speed = 60 km/h, x = 30 km/h, y = 45 km/h, find z .
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Total Distance = 60 + 90 + 120 = 270 km

Total Time = 270 ÷ 60 = 4.5 hours

Time taken for first two parts = (60 ÷ 30) + (90 ÷ 45) = 2 + 2 = 4 hours

Remaining time for z = 4.5 − 4 = 0.5 hours ⇒ z = 120 ÷ 0.5 = 240 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 240 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance₁ (d₁) = 60 km, Speed₁ (x) = 30 km/h

Distance₂ (d₂) = 90 km, Speed₂ (y) = 45 km/h

Distance₃ (d₃) = 120 km, Speed₃ (z) = ?

Average Speed (Vₐvg) = 60 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Average Speed = (Total Distance) ÷ (Total Time)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d768ca7b9f5ff7aa282bb9f9e71cad8439f23fb60f8e62859f8c5d27345ad80f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 60 + 90 + 120 = 270 km

⇒ Total Time (T) = Total Distance ÷ Average Speed

⇒ T = 270 ÷ 60 = 4.5 hours

⇒ Time for 1st segment (t₁) = 60 ÷ 30 = 2 hours

⇒ Time for 2nd segment (t₂) = 90 ÷ 45 = 2 hours

⇒ Time for 3rd segment (t₃) = T − (t₁ + t₂)

⇒ t₃ = 4.5 − (2 + 2) = 4.5 − 4 = 0.5 hours

⇒ Speed z = Distance₃ ÷ t₃

⇒ z = 120 ÷ 0.5 = 240 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 240 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Equal Distances

If two equal distances are covered at speeds u and v, then Average Speed = 2uv ÷ (u + v).

Conversion of Speed Units

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Relative Speed

If two bodies move at speeds u and v, relative speed is (u + v) in opposite directions and (u − v) in the same direction.

questions.question: A shopkeeper sells a shirt for ₹1200 and incurs a loss of 40\% . At what price should he sell the shirt to gain 10\% ?

questions.question: A dealer professes to sell goods at a loss of 10\% but uses a weight of 750 { g} instead of 1 { kg} . What is his real gain or loss percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the effective ratio method: Price Ratio × Weight Ratio = Final Ratio

Professed Price (10% loss) → 100 : 90 ⇒ 10 : 9

Weight Deception (750g instead of 1000g) → 750 : 1000 ⇒ 3 : 4

Overall Ratio (CP : SP) → (10 × 3) : (9 × 4) ⇒ 30 : 36 ⇒ 5 : 6

Profit % = (Difference / CP) × 100 = (1 / 5) × 100 = 20% profit.

**∴ The correct answer is 20% profit.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

True weight = 1000 g

False weight used = 750 g

Professed loss percentage = 10%

**Formula Used:**

Actual CP = Cost of the weight actually given to the customer.

Actual SP = Price at which the customer buys the professed quantity.

Gain % = [(SP − CP) / CP] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cada382c5edf656faa65b91920d896b646f0bf04fe0dfa62aa5415cc64c95b85.png] 

Let the cost price (CP) of 1000 g be ₹1000.

⇒ Professed selling price (SP) = 1000 − (10% of 1000)

⇒ Professed SP = 1000 − 100 = ₹900

⇒ Dealer uses a weight of 750 g instead of 1000 g.

⇒ Actual CP of the goods delivered = ₹750

⇒ Actual Profit = Actual SP − Actual CP = 900 − 750 = ₹150

⇒ Real Gain % = (150 / 750) × 100

⇒ Real Gain % = (1 / 5) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20% profit.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Dishonest Dealer Weight Gain

If a dealer sells at CP but uses false weight, Gain % = [Error / (True Weight − Error)] × 100.

Combined Profit/Loss Ratio

Net Ratio = (100 + Gain₁% / 100) × (True Weight / False Weight). If loss, use (100 − Loss%).

Successive Percentage Change

Total Change = [x + y + (xy / 100)]% where x and y are individual percentage changes.

questions.question: ₹1250 is divided between A and B such that the amount of A to the amount of B is 12:13 . What are the amounts received by A and B?

⇒ Total ratio = 12 + 13 = 25

⇒ Amount received by A = 12 × 50 = ₹600

⇒ Amount received by B = (13 ÷ 25) × 1250

Ratio Distribution Rule

Mean Proportional

Duplicate and Sub-duplicate Ratio

The duplicate ratio of a:b is a²:b² and the sub-duplicate ratio is √a:√b.

questions.question: Two numbers are in the ratio 5:8 , and their HCF is 6 . Find the numbers.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Numbers in ratio = 5 : 8

HCF of numbers = 6

Numbers = Ratio parts × HCF

Required numbers = (5 × 6) and (8 × 6)

Required numbers = 30 and 48

**∴ The correct answer is 30, 48.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of two numbers = 5 : 8

Highest Common Factor (HCF) = 6

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ffc8484737783d36987a13d4602a5f8b7ee56317bfb34f9e74a03ed01328d678.png] 

**Formula Used:**

If two numbers are in the ratio a : b and their HCF is x, then the numbers are ax and bx.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the two numbers be 5x and 8x.

⇒ Since 5 and 8 are co-prime (their common factor is 1), the HCF of 5x and 8x is x.

⇒ Given that HCF = 6.

⇒ ∴ x = 6

⇒ First number = 5x = 5 × 6 = 30

⇒ Second number = 8x = 8 × 6 = 48

**∴ The correct answer is 30, 48.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF and Ratio Property

When numbers are expressed in their simplest ratio a : b, the factor that was divided out is their HCF. Thus, Numbers = HCF × a and HCF × b.

LCM from HCF and Ratio

The Least Common Multiple (LCM) of two numbers in ratio a : b with HCF 'H' is given by LCM = H × a × b.

HCF × LCM Relation

For any two numbers, the product of the numbers is always equal to the product of their HCF and LCM. (n₁ × n₂ = HCF × LCM).

questions.question: Two candidates appeared for an examination. The marks obtained by one candidate exceeded those of the other by 75 . Moreover, his score was equivalent to 80\% of the combined marks of both candidates. Determine the marks obtained by each candidate.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Candidate A marks to Total marks = 80% = 4 : 5

Candidate B marks = Total − Candidate A = 5 − 4 = 1 unit

Difference in marks = 4 − 1 = 3 units

Given 3 units = 75 ⇒ 1 unit = 25

Marks = 4 × 25 and 1 × 25 = 100 and 25

**∴ The correct answer is 25 and 100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Difference between marks = 75

Candidate A marks = 80% of (A + B)

**Formula:**

Percentage Value = (Part / Total) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f1844e13b9e89ff65a48fff3da18839a30e9ff3a67b1b400237a67fecf63bf7f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let total marks of both candidates be x.

⇒ Marks of Candidate A = 80% of x = 0.8x

⇒ Marks of Candidate B = x − 0.8x = 0.2x

⇒ Difference = 0.8x − 0.2x = 75

⇒ 0.6x = 75

⇒ x = 75 ÷ 0.6 = 125

⇒ Marks of Candidate A = 0.8 × 125 = 100

⇒ Marks of Candidate B = 0.2 × 125 = 25

**∴ The correct answer is 25 and 100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage to Ratio Conversion

To simplify calculations, convert percentages to fractions (e.g., 80% = 4/5, 20% = 1/5, 60% = 3/5).

Total Sum Concept

When one part is given as a percentage of the total, the other part is (100 − given percentage) of that same total.

Base Value Identification

Always identify whether the percentage is calculated on the total or on another individual value to avoid calculation errors.

questions.question: In an election, there were only two candidates. One of the candidates secured 40\% of the votes and was defeated by the other candidate by 4,65,104 votes. What is the total number of votes polled?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Winner secured 100% − 40% = 60% of votes.

Victory margin = 60% − 40% = 20%.

20% of total votes = 4,65,104.

100% of total votes = 4,65,104 × 5 = 23,25,520.

**∴ The correct answer is 23,25,520.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Percentage of votes secured by the defeated candidate = 40%

Margin of defeat = 4,65,104 votes

**Formula Used:**

Total Votes = (Vote Difference ÷ Percentage Difference) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1d3f9322b7840d22f9bb6f6288b5e699d6d0ea596dc6e2455ed4f230d616f885.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the total number of votes polled be x.

⇒ Votes of the defeated candidate = 40% of x = 0.40x

⇒ Votes of the winning candidate = (100 − 40)% of x = 60% of x = 0.60x

⇒ Difference in votes = 0.60x − 0.40x = 0.20x

⇒ 0.20x = 4,65,104

⇒ x = 4,65,104 ÷ 0.20

⇒ x = 4,65,104 × 5

⇒ x = 23,25,520

**∴ The correct answer is 23,25,520.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Winning Margin

The winning margin is the difference between the votes obtained by the winner and the runner-up. Margin = Winner's Votes − Runner-up's Votes.

Invalid Votes

If invalid votes are present, the calculation for the winner/loser is usually based on the Valid Votes. Total Votes = Valid Votes + Invalid Votes.

Percentage Change Rule

To find the total from a percentage part: Total = (Part Value ÷ Percentage of Part) × 100.

questions.question: Rohan sells a bed by giving a 65\% discount on its list price. If instead, he had given only a 62\% discount, the selling price would have been ₹6,000 more. What is the original marked price of the bed?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The difference in discount percentages reflects the difference in selling prices.

Difference in discount % = 65% − 62% = 3%

This 3% of Marked Price corresponds to the increase in Selling Price = ₹6,000

⇒ 3% of Marked Price = ₹6,000

⇒ Marked Price = (6,000 ÷ 3) × 100 = ₹2,00,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,00,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/98d1af265260e1120c3d190542f3c400ad02b8b61e9d1345376413d165b9342c.png] 

**Given:**

Discount 1 = 65%

Discount 2 = 62%

Difference in Selling Price = ₹6,000

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price (MP) × (100 − Discount%)/100

**Calculations:**

Let the Marked Price of the bed be ₹x.

⇒ Selling Price in first case (SP₁) = x × (100 − 65)/100 = 0.35x

⇒ Selling Price in second case (SP₂) = x × (100 − 62)/100 = 0.38x

According to the question, the difference in selling prices is ₹6,000:

⇒ SP₂ − SP₁ = 6,000

⇒ 0.38x − 0.35x = 6,000

⇒ 0.03x = 6,000

⇒ x = 6,000 ÷ 0.03

⇒ x = 6,00,000 ÷ 3

⇒ x = 2,00,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,00,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relationship between MP and Discount

Marked Price is the price listed on the product. Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price. Discount = MP − SP.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount is given by (a + b − (a × b)/100)%.

Discount Percentage Formula

Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100. This is used to find the rate of reduction offered on the list price.

questions.question: Manish sells a parcel of land for ₹2,20,000 after giving a rebate of 45\% on its original listed price. What was the original valuation of the land before the rebate was applied?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Rebate 45% = 9/20 in fraction → Original = 20 units, Rebate = 9 units

Selling Price = 20 − 9 = 11 units

11 units = ₹2,20,000 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹20,000

Original Valuation = 20 units × ₹20,000 = ₹4,00,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4,00,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price (SP) = ₹2,20,000

Rebate (Discount) = 45%

**Formula Used:**

Original Valuation = [Selling Price ÷ (100 − Rebate %)] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/059b8742d891395c35fc9dd27fe39efee9c50580927326a611fc08873d8dca2a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Percentage of original price paid = 100% − 45% = 55%

⇒ Let Original Valuation be P.

⇒ 55% of P = ₹2,20,000

⇒ (55 ÷ 100) × P = 2,20,000

⇒ P = (2,20,000 × 100) ÷ 55

⇒ P = 4,000 × 100

questions.question: In what form was 'Vetti' tax collected during the Chola period?
questions.solution:
pThe correct answer is __**Forced labour**__.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Chola dynasty**, which ruled major parts of **South India** between the **9th and 13th centuries**, maintained a highly sophisticated and detailed taxation system.
 
• Inscriptions from the Chola period, especially those found in **Tamil Nadu**, mention more than **400 different terms** for various types of taxes levied by the state.
 
• The tax known as **Vetti** was a form of **forced labour**. Unlike other taxes, it was not collected in the form of **cash**, **gold**, or **grain**; instead, the common people were compelled to provide free labor for state projects or for the local landlords.
 
• Another primary tax was **Kadamai**, which refers to **land revenue**. This was the most important source of income for the **Chola administration** and was typically paid by the cultivators from their agricultural produce.
 
• The existence of **Vetti** highlights the administrative control of the **Chola rulers** over the physical labor of their subjects, which was often utilized for constructing massive **temples**, **irrigation tanks**, and **roads**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chola Land Classification**: The inscriptions classify land into distinct categories based on ownership and purpose. These include **Vellanvagai** (land held by non-Brahmana peasant proprietors), **Brahmadeya** (land gifted to Brahmanas), **Shalabhoga** (land for the maintenance of a school), and **Devadana** (land gifted to temples).
 
• **Local Self-Government**: The Cholas were pioneers in **local self-administration**. The **Uttaramerur inscription** provides a detailed account of how the **Sabha** (assembly of Brahmanas) and the **Ur** (village assembly) functioned, including the criteria for membership and the method of election using the **Kudavolai system** (pot-ticket system).
 
• **Economic Activities**: Apart from land revenue and forced labor, the state collected taxes on **thatching the house**, the use of **ladders** to climb palmyra trees, and a cess on **succession to family property**. These diverse taxes ensured a steady flow of wealth to the royal treasury.
 
• **Imperial Expansion**: Powerful rulers like **Rajaraja I** and **Rajendra I** used the empire's vast resources to build a formidable **navy**, which allowed them to expand their influence to the **Maldives**, **Sri Lanka**, and parts of **Southeast Asia**.
 
• **Cultural Contributions**: The revenue generated from taxes like **Kadamai** funded the construction of architectural marvels such as the **Brihadisvara Temple** at **Thanjavur**, built by **Rajaraja I** in **1010 AD**, which stands as a symbol of Chola power and devotion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Chola inscriptions** are the primary historical source for understanding their fiscal policy. They reflect a transition from a **tribal-chiefdom** structure to a highly **centralized imperial state**.
 
• While **Vetti** involved physical labor, the state also ensured that the **peasantry** was productive by investing heavily in **irrigation projects**, such as the **anicut** (dams) built across the **Kaveri River**.
 
• The **forced labour** system was not unique to the Cholas but was exceptionally well-documented in their **epigraphical records**, showing how the state mobilized human resources for public works and religious monuments.

questions.question: Under the Zabt system of Mughal empire, how was tax determined?

options.text: Based on crop yields, prices and area cultivated
Based on fixed percentage of the crop yield
Based on fixed annual amount per farmer

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Based on crop yields, prices and area cultivated**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Zabt system** was a significant land revenue system introduced during the reign of the **Mughal Emperor Akbar**. It was primarily developed and implemented by his finance minister, **Raja Todar Mal**, around the year **1580**.
 
• Under this system, the **revenue** was determined after a very careful survey of **crop yields**, **market prices**, and the **area of land cultivated** over a continuous period of **ten years** (from **1570 to 1580**).
 
• Each crop had its own schedule of revenue rates, known as **Dastur-i-Amal**. The state's share was generally fixed at **one-third** of the average produce, which was converted into **cash** based on prevailing market prices. ***Hence, the statement that tax was determined based on crop yields, prices, and area cultivated is correct.***
 
• The **Zabt system** was applied in those provinces where the Mughal administration could carry out land surveys and maintain detailed accounts, such as **Delhi**, **Agra**, **Awadh**, **Allahabad**, **Malwa**, and **Lahore**.
 
• It was also known as the **Dahshala system** because it relied on the average statistics of **ten years** (Dah meaning ten) to provide stability to both the state and the cultivators.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Classification of Land:** For the purpose of revenue assessment under **Akbar**, land was divided into four categories based on the continuity of cultivation:

 
 
• **Polaj**: Land which was annually cultivated for each crop in succession and never allowed to lie fallow.
 
• **Parauti**: Land left out of cultivation for a time (**1 or 2 years**) that it might recover its strength.
 
• **Chachar**: Land that had lain fallow for **3 or 4 years**.
 
• **Banjar**: Land uncultivated for **5 years** or more.
 
 
 
• **Land Measurement:** To ensure precision, **Akbar** replaced the old hempen rope with a new measuring unit called the **Gaj-i-Ilahi** (a yard of **41 digits** or about **33 inches**) and used a **Tanab** (measuring chain) made of **Bamboo** sticks joined by iron rings.
 
• **Administrative Officers:** The collection was overseen by officials such as the **Amalguzar** (revenue collector) and the **Bitikchi** (accountant). At the local level, the **Kanungo** maintained the records of **area cultivated** and **local prices**.
 
• **Geographical Limitations:** The **Zabt** system could not be implemented in provinces like **Gujarat** and **Bengal** because the administration found it difficult to conduct regular surveys and keep track of fluctuating **crop yields** in those terrains.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Cash Collection:** Unlike earlier systems where revenue was often paid in kind, the **Zabt system** prioritized collection in **cash**. This necessitated the expansion of **local markets** and the **monetization** of the rural economy.
 
• **Raja Todar Mal:** Before serving **Akbar**, **Raja Todar Mal** had worked under **Sher Shah Suri**, where he gained initial experience in land measurement and revenue reforms, which he later perfected during the **Mughal era**.
 
• **Impact on Peasants:** While the system brought transparency, the requirement to pay in **cash** often forced peasants to sell their produce immediately after harvest, sometimes at lower prices, to meet the state's **revenue demand**.
 
• **Mansabdari Link:** The revenue collected through the **Zabt system** was used to pay the salaries of the **Mansabdars** and maintain the massive military machinery of the **Mughal Empire**.

questions.question: Which of the following part of the Indian constitution deals with the Municipalities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Part – IXA**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Part IXA** was added to the **Constitution of India** through the **74th Constitutional Amendment Act** of **1992**, which came into force on **June 1, 1993**.
 
• This part deals exclusively with **Municipalities** (Urban Local Bodies) and contains provisions from **Article 243-P to Article 243-ZG**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Part – IXA.***
 
• The act gave **constitutional status** to municipalities, making them a part of the formal democratic structure of India and ensuring they are governed by mandatory constitutional provisions.
 
• Under this part, the **12th Schedule** was added to the Constitution, which specifies **18 functional items** that fall under the jurisdiction of municipalities, such as urban planning, regulation of land use, and public health.
 
• The amendment provides for three types of Municipalities: **Nagar Panchayats** for transitional areas, **Municipal Councils** for smaller urban areas, and **Municipal Corporations** for larger urban areas.
 
• It also mandates the **reservation of seats** for Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST) in proportion to their population, and **not less than one-third** of the total number of seats for **women**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Part XIV of the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• This part covers **Services Under the Union and the States**, spanning from **Article 308 to Article 323**.
 
• It includes provisions related to the **All India Services**, recruitment, and conditions of service for persons serving the Union or a State.
 
• It also establishes the **Public Service Commissions** (UPSC and State PSCs) under **Articles 315 to 323**, ensuring independent recruitment for civil services.
 
 
 
• **Part XVII of the Indian Constitution:**
 
 
• This part deals with **Official Languages** and consists of **Articles 343 to 351**.
 
• It specifies **Hindi in Devanagari script** as the official language of the Union (**Article 343**) and contains provisions for regional languages and the language of the **Supreme Court and High Courts**.
 
• It also includes **Article 351**, which provides a directive for the **development and promotion of the Hindi language**.
 
 
 
• **Part XII of the Indian Constitution:**
 
 
• This part is titled **Finance, Property, Contracts, and Suits** and covers **Articles 264 to 300A**.
 
• It manages the **distribution of revenues** between the Union and the States, including the establishment of the **Finance Commission** under **Article 280**.
 
• Importantly, **Article 300A** was added to this part by the **44th Amendment Act, 1978**, which converted the **Right to Property** from a Fundamental Right into a **Legal Right**.
 
 
 
• **Part IX of the Indian Constitution:**
 
 
• Distinct from Part IXA, **Part IX** deals with the **Panchayats** (Rural Local Bodies).
 
• It was inserted by the **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992**, and covers **Article 243 to Article 243-O**.
 
• It added the **11th Schedule** to the Constitution, containing **29 functional items** for rural self-governance.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **State Election Commission:** Under **Article 243-K and 243-ZA**, the superintendence, direction, and control of the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of all elections to the **Panchayats and Municipalities** are vested in the **State Election Commission**.
 
• **Duration:** Both Panchayats and Municipalities are provided a fixed **five-year term**. If dissolved earlier, elections must be held within **6 months** from the date of dissolution.
 
• **District Planning Committee:** **Article 243-ZD** mandates the constitution of a **District Planning Committee** in every state to consolidate the plans prepared by the Panchayats and the Municipalities in the district.

questions.question: The sun rises about ______ hour earlier in the east (Arunachal Pradesh) than in the west (Gujarat).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**two**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **sun rises** about **two** hours earlier in **Arunachal Pradesh** (the easternmost point) than in **Gujarat** (the westernmost point) due to the vast **longitudinal extent** of India.
 
• India is situated between longitudes **68°7' E** and **97°25' E**, which results in a longitudinal difference of approximately **30 degrees**.
 
• The **Earth** takes **24 hours** to complete one full rotation of **360 degrees**. This means it takes **4 minutes** for the sun to move across **1 degree** of longitude ($1440 \text{ minutes} / 360 \text{ degrees} = 4 \text{ minutes/degree}$).
 
• Calculating the time lag for the **30-degree** difference: $30 \times 4 = 120 \text{ minutes}$, which is equivalent to **2 hours**.
 
• Because of this time difference, while it is **sunrise** in the east at **Arunachal Pradesh**, it is still dark in the west at **Gujarat** for another **120 minutes**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Standard Meridian of India**:

 
 
• To avoid confusion caused by different local times within the country, a **Standard Meridian** is chosen. For India, this is **82°30' E**.
 
• The local time at this meridian is accepted as the **Indian Standard Time (IST)** for the entire **country**.
 
• This meridian passes through **Mirzapur** in **Uttar Pradesh** (and also through parts of **Madhya Pradesh**, **Chhattisgarh**, **Odisha**, and **Andhra Pradesh**).
 
 
 
• **Geographical Extent**:
 
 
• India's **latitudinal extent** is between **8°4' N** and **37°6' N**.
 
• The **Tropic of Cancer** (**23°30' N**) divides the country into almost two equal parts.
 
• The total **area** of the Indian landmass is about **3.28 million square km**, making it the **seventh** largest country in the world by area.
 
 
 
• **Greenwich Mean Time (GMT)**:
 
 
• **Indian Standard Time (IST)** is **5 hours and 30 minutes** ahead of **Greenwich Mean Time (GMT)**.
 
• When it is **12:00 PM** at **Greenwich** (**0° longitude**), it is **5:30 PM** in **India**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **easternmost point** of India is a small town called **Kibithu** in **Arunachal Pradesh**, located at approximately **97°25' E**.
 
• The **westernmost point** of India is **Guahar Moti** in the **Kutch** district of **Gujarat**, located at approximately **68°7' E**.
 
• Despite the **two-hour** time lag in sunrise and sunset between these two points, the **clocks** in both states show the same time because India follows a **single time zone**.
 
• There have been recurring demands for a separate **time zone** (often called the **ChaiBagaan Time**) for the **North-Eastern states** to save daylight and improve **productivity**, as the sun sets very early in those **locations**.

questions.question: The longitudinal valley lying between lesser Himalaya and the Shiwaliks is known as _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**duns**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The longitudinal valleys that lie between the **Lesser Himalayas** (also known as **Himachal**) and the **Shiwaliks** (the outermost range) are locally known as **Duns**.
 
• These valleys were formed when the rivers flowing from the higher Himalayan ranges were temporarily obstructed by the rising **Shiwalik range**, leading to the formation of temporary lakes. Over time, these lakes were drained as the rivers cut through the ranges, leaving behind flat-bottomed valleys covered with **thick gravel** and **alluvium**.
 
• Some of the most prominent examples of these valleys include **Dehra Dun**, **Kotli Dun**, and **Patli Dun**.
 
• **Dehra Dun** is the largest of these valleys, with an approximate length of **35 to 45 km** and a width ranging between **22 and 25 km**. It serves as a significant administrative and educational hub in **Uttarakhand**.
 
• Geographically, these **Duns** are characterized by their fertile soil, making them highly suitable for **agriculture** and **human settlement** compared to the rugged slopes of the surrounding mountains.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Shiwaliks (Outer Himalayas):**

 
 
• This is the southernmost range of the **Himalayas**. It extends over a width of **10 to 50 km** and has an altitude varying between **900 and 1100 metres**.
 
• The **Shiwaliks** are composed of **unconsolidated sediments** brought down by rivers from the main Himalayan ranges located further north.
 
 
 
• **Doabs:**
 
 
• The term **Doab** refers to the fertile land situated **between two converging rivers**. In Persian, **"Do"** means two and **"Ab"** means water.
 
• An example is the **Bari Doab**, which lies between the **Beas** and the **Ravi** rivers in the **Punjab** region.
 
 
 
• **Ranns:**
 
 
• The term **Rann** typically refers to a **salt marsh** or saline mudflat. The most famous is the **Rann of Kutch** located in **Gujarat**, India.
 
• It is one of the largest **salt deserts** in the world and is known for its unique ecosystem and the **Great Rann of Kutch** festival.
 
 
 
• **Lesser Himalayas (Himachal):**
 
 
• Located north of the **Shiwaliks**, this range is mainly composed of highly compressed and altered rocks. The altitude varies from **3,700 to 4,500 metres**.
 
• This region is home to famous hill stations like **Shimla**, **Mussoorie**, and **Nainital**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Himalayan mountains** are divided into three main parallel ranges: the **Great Himalayas (Himadri)**, the **Lesser Himalayas (Himachal)**, and the **Outer Himalayas (Shiwaliks)**.
 
• The **Duns** are specifically associated with the transition zone between the **middle** and **outer** ranges.
 
• The formation of **Duns** is a result of **tectonic activity** and **fluvial erosion** and deposition that occurred during the **Pleistocene epoch**.
 
• While **Dehra Dun** is the most famous, other smaller duns like **Pinjore Dun** in Haryana also exist, providing vital flat land in the hilly terrain.

questions.question: What is the pressure of blood of human body inside the artery during ventricular systole called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Systolic pressure**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Systolic pressure** is defined as the maximum pressure exerted by the blood against the walls of the **arteries** during the contraction of the heart's **ventricles**.
 
• This phase of the cardiac cycle is known as **ventricular systole**, during which blood is forcefully pumped into the **aorta** and **pulmonary artery**.
 
• In a healthy adult human, the normal **systolic pressure** is approximately **120 mmHg** (millimeters of mercury).
 
• It represents the "top number" in a standard blood pressure reading (e.g., 120/80 mmHg) and reflects the force of the **heartbeat**.
 
• The **systolic pressure** increases during physical activity, **stress**, or excitement as the heart works harder to deliver **oxygenated blood** to the body's tissues.

questions.question: Vanji', identified with present-day Karur in Tamil Nadu, was the capital of which dynasty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chera**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vanji**, historically identified with modern-day **Karur** in **Tamil Nadu**, served as the inland capital of the early **Chera** dynasty during the **Sangam Age** (approx. **3rd century BCE** to **3rd century CE**).
 
• The **Cheras** were one of the three powerful dynasties of ancient **South India**, collectively known as the **Muventar** (Three Crowned Kings), alongside the **Cholas** and the **Pandyas**.
 
• Geographically, the **Chera** kingdom occupied the central and northern parts of **Kerala** and the **Kongu Nadu** region of **Tamil Nadu**. **Karur** is situated on the banks of the **Amaravati River**, which is a tributary of the **Cauvery**.
 
• The Greek geographer **Ptolemy**, writing in the **2nd century CE**, referred to **Karur** as "**Karoura**," identifying it as an important royal residence and inland capital of the **Cheras**.
 
• Archaeological excavations at **Karur** have yielded a significant number of **Roman coins**, **pottery**, and **inscriptions**, proving its status as a flourishing center for **international trade** and **metallurgy** during antiquity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chera Dynasty Details**:

 
 
• The royal emblem of the **Cheras** was the **Bow and Arrow**.
 
• Apart from **Vanji**, their major port cities on the western coast were **Musiri** (Muchiri) and **Tondi**, which were vital for the **pepper trade** with the **Roman Empire**.
 
• Famous rulers include **Nedunjeral Adan** and **Senguttuvan** (the Red Chera), who is celebrated in the epic **Silappadikaram** for establishing the **Pattini cult**.
 
 
 
• **Haryanka Dynasty**:
 
 
• This was the first important ruling dynasty of **Magadha** in ancient **North India**, founded by **Bimbisara** around **544 BCE**.
 
• Their capital was initially **Girivraja** (Rajgir) and was later shifted to **Pataliputra**. This dynasty is not associated with the **Tamil** region or **Karur**.
 
 
 
• **Pallava Dynasty**:
 
 
• The **Pallavas** emerged as a formidable power in the **4th century CE**, with their capital located at **Kanchipuram** in northern **Tamil Nadu**.
 
• They are renowned for **Dravidian architecture**, particularly the rock-cut temples and the **Shore Temple** at **Mahabalipuram**.
 
 
 
• **Rashtrakuta Dynasty**:
 
 
• Founded by **Dantidurga** in the **8th century CE**, this dynasty ruled large parts of the **Deccan**.
 
• Their capital was **Manyakheta** (modern-day **Malkhed** in **Karnataka**). They are famous for the monolithic **Kailasa Temple** at **Ellora**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Sangam Literature**: Sources like the **Purananuru** and **Pathitrupathu** provide extensive details about the **Chera** kings, their military exploits, and the prosperity of **Vanji**.
 
• **Pugalur Inscriptions**: These **Brahmi inscriptions** found near **Karur** (dated to the **1st-2nd century CE**) mention three generations of **Chera** kings of the **Irumporai** line, providing epigraphic evidence for the dynasty's rule in this specific location.
 
• **Trade Significance**: **Karur** was a strategic point for the movement of goods between the **Malabar Coast** and the **Coromandel Coast**, making it a wealthy administrative and commercial hub.

questions.question: At age of ____, Siddhārtha Gautama asked to be driven through the city in a chariot, and for the first time in his life came across an old man, a sick man, and a dead body.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**29**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Siddhartha Gautama**, the founder of Buddhism, was born as a prince in the **Shakya clan**. For the first **29 years** of his life, he lived in complete seclusion and luxury within the palace walls of **Kapilavastu**, shielded from the realities of human suffering.
 
• At the **age of 29**, he felt a deep curiosity to see the world outside his royal residence. He convinced his charioteer, **Channa**, to take him on a series of outings through the city.
 
• During these journeys, he encountered what are known in Buddhist tradition as the **Four Sights**. These sights included an **old man** (representing the decay of the body), a **sick man** (representing the fragility of health), and a **dead body** (representing the inevitability of death).
 
• The fourth sight he encountered was a **wandering ascetic** or monk, who appeared peaceful despite having no worldly possessions. This final sight suggested to him that there was a way to overcome the universal problem of suffering.
 
• These experiences led to a profound spiritual crisis, prompting him to leave his wife **Yashodhara** and newborn son **Rahula** to seek a solution to the cycle of birth, aging, and death. This event is historically referred to as the **Great Renunciation** or **Mahabhinishkramana**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Early Life and Birth**: Siddhartha was born in **Lumbini** (in present-day **Nepal**) around **563 BCE**. His father was **King Suddhodana** and his mother was **Queen Maya**. It was prophesied at his birth that he would either become a great king or a great spiritual leader.
 
• **Attainment of Enlightenment**: After wandering for **six years** as an ascetic, Siddhartha sat under a **Pipal tree** (later known as the **Bodhi Tree**) in **Bodh Gaya**, Bihar. At the **age of 35**, he attained **Nirvana** (enlightenment) and became the **Buddha**, which means the "Enlightened One" or the "Awakened One."
 
• **The First Sermon**: He delivered his first discourse at **Sarnath**, near **Varanasi**. This event is known as **Dharmachakrapravartana** (Setting the Wheel of Dharma in motion). He taught the **Four Noble Truths** and the **Eightfold Path** to his first five disciples.
 
• **Teachings on Suffering**: The core of his philosophy was **Dukkha** (suffering). He taught that desire (**Tanha**) is the root cause of suffering and that by following the "Middle Path"—avoiding both extreme self-indulgence and extreme self-mortification—one could achieve liberation.
 
• **Mahaparinirvana**: The Buddha spent the remaining **45 years** of his life traveling across the Indo-Gangetic plain, teaching and organizing his followers into the **Sangha**. He passed away at the **age of 80** in **Kushinagar**, an event known as **Mahaparinirvana**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of the Age 29**: This particular **year** marks the transition from his life as a **prince** to his life as a **seeker of truth**. It highlights the contrast between worldly attachment and the quest for spiritual liberation.
 
• **Cultural Impact**: The story of the **Four Sights** is a central theme in Buddhist art and literature, serving as a powerful allegory for the awakening of human consciousness to the reality of **impermanence**.
 
• **Geographical Context**: Most of the key events of the Buddha's life took place in the modern-day Indian states of **Bihar** and **Uttar Pradesh**, as well as the **Terai** region of **Nepal**.

questions.question: Theru Koothu' is a traditional night-time theatre form of which Indian state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Theru Koothu** is a traditional folk theatre form that originates from and is primarily practiced in the Indian state of **Tamil Nadu**.
 
• The name is derived from the **Tamil** words **'Theru'**, meaning **street**, and **'Koothu'**, meaning **theatre** or **play**. As the name suggests, it is traditionally performed in open streets or public squares.
 
• It is an **extemporaneous** form of art where the performers engage in a combination of **songs**, **spoken dialogues**, and **dance** movements to narrate mythological stories.
 
• The themes of **Theru Koothu** are mostly drawn from the **Indian epics**, specifically the **Mahabharata** and the **Ramayana**, along with local folk legends.
 
• Performances are usually held during **temple festivals**, particularly during the months of **Panguni** and **Aadi** (roughly **March to August**), and they often take place at **night**, lasting until **dawn**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Regional Theatre Forms in Other States:**

 
 
• **Goa:** One of the most famous traditional theatre forms in **Goa** is **Dashavatara**, which focuses on the ten incarnations of **Lord Vishnu**. It is also prevalent in the **Konkan** region of **Maharashtra**.
 
• **Odisha:** This state is home to **Jatra**, a popular folk theatre, and **Prahlad Natak**, which is characterized by high-pitched singing and classical music. **Odisha** is also famous for **Chhau**, a semi-classical dance-drama.
 
• **Arunachal Pradesh:** The state features tribal mask dances and folk dramas like **Aji Lamu** (performed by the **Monpa** tribe), which often incorporate **Buddhist** themes and folklore.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Tamil Folk Arts:**
 
 
• **Tamil Nadu** has a rich history of folk performances including **Karagattam** (balancing pots), **Kavadi Aattam** (ceremonial sacrifice), and **Oyilattam** (dance of grace).
 
• In **Theru Koothu**, the **Kattiakaran** serves as the **Sutradhara** or narrator who introduces the play, provides comic relief, and bridges the gap between the actors and the audience.
 
• Instruments used in these performances typically include the **Mridangam**, **Thalam** (cymbals), and the **Mukhavina** (a wind instrument similar to the **Nadaswaram**).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Costumes and Makeup:** The performers wear **elaborate costumes**, including **large wooden headgears** (Kiridams) and **heavy makeup**, to ensure they are visible and their characters are recognizable to a large crowd in an open setting.
 
• **Ritual Significance:** **Theru Koothu** is often associated with the cult of **Draupadi Amman**. In many villages, the performance is a **ritualistic offering** to the goddess for a good harvest or to ward off diseases.
 
• **Duration:** A typical **Theru Koothu** festival can span over **18 days**, mirroring the **18-day Kurukshetra War** described in the **Mahabharata**.
 
• **Evolution:** While it remains a rural folk art, modern adaptations have seen **Theru Koothu** being used to spread **social awareness** regarding health, education, and government schemes in **Tamil Nadu**.

questions.question: In Gujarat, the 'Rann Utsav' is held in which region?
questions.solution:

• **Rann Utsav** is a grand winter festival celebrated in the **Kutch** district of **Gujarat**, India.
 
• The festival is primarily held at **Dhordo**, a village that serves as the gateway to the **Great Rann of Kutch**, which is one of the largest salt deserts in the world.
 
• This cultural extravaganza was conceptualized in **2005** by the then-Chief Minister of Gujarat, **Shri Narendra Modi**, to promote tourism in the region after the devastating earthquake of **2001**.
 
• The celebration typically spans from **November** to **February** or **March**, coinciding with the winter season when the weather is pleasant for tourists.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Kutch District**:

 
 
• It is the **largest district** in India by geographical area, covering approximately **45,674 square kilometers**.
 
• The region is divided into the **Great Rann of Kutch** and the **Little Rann of Kutch**, the latter being the only home to the **Indian Wild Ass** (Khur).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

questions.question: What happened to Bahadur Shah Zafar after the revolt of 1857 was put down by the British East India Company?

options.text: He was forced to leave the kingdom.
He was made a puppet ruler.
He was made the emperor again.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**He was forced to leave the kingdom**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bahadur Shah Zafar**, the last **Mughal Emperor**, was the figurehead leader of the **Revolt of 1857**. After the British forces successfully suppressed the uprising and recaptured **Delhi** in **September 1857**, he was captured at **Humayun's Tomb**.
 
• Following his capture by **Major William Hodson**, he was brought to trial at the **Red Fort**. He was found **guilty** of aiding and abetting the mutineers and for proclaiming himself the **Emperor of Hindustan** against the **British East India Company**.
 
• Instead of being allowed to remain in his kingdom as a puppet or a nominal head, the British decided to dismantle the **Mughal Dynasty** entirely. He was **exiled** to **Rangoon** (in present-day **Myanmar**) along with his wife, **Begum Zinat Mahal**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The British authorities ensured he had no political power or hope of return. He lived the remainder of his life in **Rangoon** as a **state prisoner** until his death on **November 7, 1862**, at the **age** of **87**. ***Hence, the correct answer is option 1.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **End of the Mughal Empire**:

 
 
• The **Government of India Act 1858** was passed in the aftermath of the revolt, transferring the governance of India from the **East India Company** to the **British Crown**.
 
• This act officially terminated the **Mughal Empire**. The British declared that **Bahadur Shah Zafar’s** successors would not be allowed to use the title of **"King"** or **"Emperor"** and would only be known as **Princes**.
 
 
 
• **Fate of the Heirs**:
 
 
• To ensure no future Mughal claimant could lead another uprising, **Major Hodson** summarily executed Zafar’s sons, **Mirza Mughal** and **Mirza Khizr Sultan**, and his grandson, **Mirza Abu Bakr**, at a site in Delhi now known as **Khooni Darwaza**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Exile**:
 
 
• The **exile** to **Burma** (Myanmar) was a strategic move to remove the symbolic head of Indian resistance from his home soil. It marked the definitive shift of **sovereignty** to the **British Empire**, with **Queen Victoria** eventually being proclaimed the **Empress of India** in **1876**.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of Zafar**:
 
 
• Beyond politics, **Bahadur Shah Zafar** was a noted **Urdu poet**. His poetry, often written under the pen name **'Zafar'**, expressed his deep grief over his **exile** and the loss of his **beloved homeland**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Capture Details**: He was apprehended on **September 21, 1857**. The British commander **Major Hodson** was instrumental in the fall of **Delhi**.
 
• **Legal Trial**: His trial lasted for **21 days**, and he was convicted on **four charges**, including rebellion and murder.
 
• **Geographical Shift**: The transition from **Delhi** to **Rangoon** symbolized the complete loss of **territorial authority** for the **Mughal lineage**.
 
• **Historical Context**: The revolt is often referred to as the **First War of Indian Independence** or the **Sepoy Mutiny**, occurring between **May 1857** and **July 1858**.

questions.question: Venus is the _______ brightest object in the sky.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3rd**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Venus** is the **third** brightest natural object in the Earth's sky, ranked only after the **Sun** and the **Moon**.
 
• Its **maximum apparent magnitude** can reach approximately **-4.6 to -4.9**, making it bright enough to be seen during the daytime under ideal atmospheric conditions.
 
• The high visibility of the planet earned it the names **Morning Star** and **Evening Star**, as it appears at its brightest shortly before **sunrise** or shortly after **sunset**.
 
• The primary reason for its extreme brightness is its **Albedo**; **Venus** reflects about **70%** of the sunlight that hits it due to a thick, permanent cover of **sulfuric acid clouds**.
 
• It is the **second planet** from the **Sun**, orbiting at an average distance of about **108 million kilometers** (approximately **0.72 Astronomical Units**).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Earth's Twin**:

 
 
• **Venus** is often referred to as **Earth's sister planet** or twin because they are very similar in **size**, **mass**, and **density**.
 
• The diameter of **Venus** is roughly **12,104 kilometers**, which is about **95%** of Earth's diameter.
 
 
 
• **Atmospheric Pressure and Temperature**:
 
 
• It possesses the **densest atmosphere** of the four terrestrial planets, consisting of over **96% carbon dioxide**.
 
• This leads to a runaway **greenhouse effect**, making it the **hottest planet** in the solar system with surface temperatures averaging **464 degrees Celsius** (**867 degrees Fahrenheit**).
 
• The **surface pressure** is about **92 times** that of Earth, equivalent to the pressure **900 meters** deep in Earth's oceans.
 
 
 
• **Unique Rotation**:
 
 
• **Venus** exhibits **retrograde rotation**, meaning it rotates on its axis from **East to West**, which is opposite to most planets in the solar system.
 
• A single **sidereal day** on **Venus** lasts about **243 Earth days**, which is actually longer than its **orbital period** (year) of **225 Earth days**.
 
 
 
• **Moons and Rings**:
 
 
• Like **Mercury**, **Venus** is unique in our solar system for having **no natural satellites** (moons) and **no planetary rings**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Phases of Venus**: Much like the **Moon**, **Venus** goes through distinct **phases**. This was first observed by **Galileo Galilei** in **1610**, providing critical evidence for the **heliocentric (Sun-centered) model** of the solar system.
 
• **Space Missions**: **Venus** was the first planet to be visited by a spacecraft (**Mariner 2** in **1962**) and the first to be successfully landed upon (**Venera 7** by the **Soviet Union** in **1970**).
 
• **Surface Features**: Radar mapping by **NASA's Magellan** mission in the **1990s** revealed a surface dominated by **volcanic activity**, **mountains** (such as **Maxwell Montes**), and vast **lava plains**.
 
• **Transits**: A **Transit of Venus** occurs when the planet passes directly between the **Earth** and the **Sun**; these are rare events that happen in pairs separated by **eight years**, with intervals of more than a **century** between pairs. The most recent transits occurred in **2004** and **2012**.

questions.question: In which year was the Mahalwari system of land revenue introduced by the British in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1822**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Mahalwari system** was a land revenue system introduced by the British in **1822**.
 
• It was devised by **Holt Mackenzie**, who believed that the village community was an important social institution in **North Indian** society that needed to be preserved.
 
• Under this system, the unit of revenue assessment was the **Mahal**, which typically referred to a **village** or a group of villages.
 
• The revenue demand was not fixed permanently; instead, it was **revised periodically** based on a detailed survey of the land, customary rights, and productivity.
 
• The task of collecting the revenue and paying it to the **East India Company** was given to the **village headman** (known as the **Lambardar**), rather than the **Zamindar**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Geographical Spread**: The **Mahalwari system** was implemented in the **North-Western Provinces** of the **Bengal Presidency** (most of which is in present-day **Uttar Pradesh**), parts of **Central India**, and the **Punjab**.
 
• **Comparison with other systems**:
 
 
• **Permanent Settlement (1793)**: Introduced by **Lord Cornwallis** in **Bengal**, **Bihar**, and **Odisha**, where the revenue was fixed forever.
 
• **Ryotwari System (1820)**: Introduced by **Thomas Munro** and **Alexander Read** in **Southern India** (**Madras** and **Bombay**), where the settlement was made directly with the **Ryots** (cultivators).
 
 
 
• **Evolution of the System**: Because the initial assessment in **1822** was found to be too complex and the revenue demand too high, **Lord William Bentinck** revised the system under the **Regulation of 1833** to make it more practical.
 
• **Impact**: While it recognized the collective nature of the village, the high revenue demands often led to the **impoverishment** of the peasantry and the forced sale of land by those who could not meet the **Company's** demands.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Year 1765**: This year marks the **Treaty of Allahabad**, through which the **British East India Company** obtained the **Diwani rights** (right to collect revenue) for **Bengal**, **Bihar**, and **Orissa**.
 
• **Year 1793**: This was the year the **Permanent Settlement** (Zamindari system) was enacted in **Bengal**, creating a class of hereditary landlords.
 
• **Year 1801**: This period saw the expansion of British territory in **North India**, specifically the **Cession of Awadh** (Oudh) territories to the **East India Company**, which later became part of the area under **Mahalwari** assessment.
 
• **Regulation VII of 1822**: This was the specific **legislative act** that gave legal validity to the **Mahalwari system** across the specified territories.

__
 
• **Sanjha** is a melodious and traditional folk song primarily associated with the **Malwa region** of **Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• It is an oral musical tradition performed exclusively by **young, unmarried girls** in groups, usually during the **evening** hours.
 
• The celebration of Sanjha takes place for **16 days** during the period of **Pitru Paksha** (the fortnight dedicated to ancestors) in the Hindu month of **Ashwin** (typically **September–October**).
 
• Along with singing, the girls create intricate **wall motifs** using **cow dung**, **colorful flowers**, **leaves**, and **vermilion**, representing various shapes like the **Sun**, **Moon**, and **Sanjha Bai** herself.
 
• The ritual and songs are dedicated to **Sanjha Devi**, a local deity, with the belief that performing these rituals will help the girls find a **good husband** and ensure a happy **married life**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Folk Music of Other States:**

• **Artistic Expression:** The tradition is a unique blend of **visual art** (wall paintings) and **performing art** (singing), reflecting the rural lifestyle and social bonds among young girls in **Central India**.

questions.question: The raga 'Sorathi' derives its name from the region located in _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gujarat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The raga **Sorathi**, also commonly referred to as **Raga Sorath**, is a prominent musical mode in **Hindustani classical music**.
 
• It derives its name directly from the **Sorath** region, which is a historical and geographical territory located in the **Saurashtra** peninsula of **Gujarat**.
 
• This raga is deeply embedded in the cultural fabric of **Western India**, particularly **Gujarat**, where it originated from local folk melodies before being systematized into the classical tradition.
 
• In the **Guru Granth Sahib**, the holy scripture of **Sikhism**, **Raag Sorat** appears as the **ninth** raga in the sequence of **31 ragas**, signifying its spiritual importance since the **15th century**.
 
• The raga is traditionally performed during the **second quarter of the night**, typically between **9:00 PM and 12:00 AM**, to evoke a specific emotional atmosphere.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Geographical Context of Sorath:**

 
 
• The **Sorath** region in **Gujarat** is famous for historical sites like the **Uparkot Fort** in **Junagadh** and the **Somnath Temple**.
 
• It is also the home of the **Asiatic Lion** in the **Gir National Park**, highlighting the region's diverse ecological and cultural significance.
 
 
 
• **Musical Characteristics:**
 
 
• Raga **Sorathi** is classified under the **Khamaj Thaat** in the **Bhatkande** system of classification.
 
• It is an **Audav-Sampurna** raga, meaning it uses **five notes** in the ascent (**Aroha**) and all **seven notes** in the descent (**Avaroha**).
 
• The notes **Gandhar (Ga)** and **Dhaivat (Dha)** are generally omitted during the ascending scale to maintain its unique melodic structure.
 
• It employs both forms of **Nishad**: the **Shuddha Ni** in the ascent and **Komal Ni** in the descent.
 
 
 
• **Mood and Application:**
 
 
• The raga is known for expressing **Shringar Rasa** (romance/devotion) and **Bhakti** (spirituality).
 
• It is frequently used in **Bhajans**, **Ghazals**, and semi-classical forms like **Thumri** due to its pleasing and accessible melodic nature.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Vadi and Samvadi:** The **Vadi** (most significant note) of Raga **Sorathi** is **Rishabh (Re)**, and the **Samvadi** (second most significant note) is **Dhaivat (Dha)** or **Pancham (Pa)**, depending on the specific **Gharana** (musical school).
 
• **Relation to other Ragas:** It bears a close resemblance to **Raga Des** and **Raga Tilak Kamod**. However, the specific movement (**Chalan**) and the emphasis on the **Rishabh** note distinguish it from others.
 
• **Historical Evolution:** The transition of **Sorathi** from a regional folk tune of **Gujarat** to a standard classical raga illustrates the "Great Tradition" of Indian music absorbing "Little Traditions" (local folk cultures).
 
• **Regional Variants:** While the classical form is standardized, various folk versions still exist in the **Saurashtra** and **Kutch** districts of **Gujarat**, often sung by local bards known as **Charans** and **Gadhvis**.

questions.question: Why are the ceilings of concert halls, conference halls, and cinema halls generally curved?

options.text: To ensure sound after reflection reaches all corners of the hall
To focus sound waves in one direction

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To ensure sound after reflection reaches all corners of the hall**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The ceilings of large venues like **concert halls**, **conference halls**, and **cinema halls** are generally designed with a **curved shape** (specifically a **concave** curvature) to act as a **reflector** for sound waves.
 
• When sound is produced on the stage, the waves travel upwards and strike the curved ceiling. Due to the **laws of reflection**, these waves are reflected downwards and spread **uniformly** across the entire width and length of the hall. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• This design ensures that even the audience members seated in the **furthest corners** or at the back of the hall can hear the sound clearly without significant loss in intensity.
 
• Curved ceilings prevent the formation of **"dead zones"** where sound might not reach if the ceiling were flat or irregular. If the ceiling were flat, much of the sound would follow a direct path or reflect in a way that creates "hot spots" in some areas and silence in others. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect as the goal is to reflect, not stop sound.***
 
• The curvature is calculated so that the **angle of incidence** and **angle of reflection** work together to cover the maximum area of the seating arrangement. ***Hence, statement 3 is partially incorrect because the goal is broad distribution, not just one narrow direction.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Soundboards:** In many professional auditoriums, a **curved soundboard** is placed behind the speaker or the musical performers. These boards are **concave**, and the source of sound is placed at the **focus** of the curve so that the reflected sound travels as a **parallel beam** toward the audience, enhancing clarity.
 
• **Reverberation:** This refers to the persistence of sound in an enclosed space due to **multiple reflections**. While a small amount of reverberation adds "warmth" to music, excessive reverberation can make speech unintelligible. Architects balance **curved ceilings** with **absorbent materials** to control the **reverberation time**.
 
• **Reflection of Sound:** Sound reflects off surfaces just like light. For a surface to reflect sound effectively, it must be **hard** and **smooth**. Ceilings are usually made of materials that facilitate this reflection, whereas walls might be treated differently.
 
• **Acoustic Materials:** To prevent unwanted echoes (which occur when the reflected sound reaches the ear after **0.1 seconds**), the walls and seats of **cinema halls** are often covered with **sound-absorbing materials** such as **compressed fiberboard**, **heavy curtains**, or **perforated acoustic panels**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect as the ceiling is specifically for reflection, while other elements are for absorption.***
 
• **Laws of Physics:** The **reflection of sound** follows the same principles as light: the incident wave, the reflected wave, and the normal at the point of incidence all lie in the **same plane**, and the **angle of incidence** is equal to the **angle of reflection**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Architectural Significance:** The **curvature** of the ceiling is a critical part of **architectural acoustics**, a field that combines physics and engineering to optimize sound quality within buildings.
 
• **Human Audibility:** For a human to distinguish an echo from the original sound, the distance between the source and the reflecting surface must be at least **17.2 meters** (assuming the speed of sound is **344 m/s** at room temperature). Large halls use curved ceilings to manage these distances and ensure **synchronous arrival** of sound.
 
• **Applications:** This principle is not only used in modern **multiplexes** but was also understood by ancient civilizations, as seen in the design of **Greek amphitheaters** and **whispering galleries** (like the one in **Gol Gumbaz** in Karnataka, India).

questions.question: The entire northern plains of India are made of ______ soil.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**alluvial**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Northern Plains** of India are primarily composed of **alluvial soil**, which has been deposited over millions of years by three major Himalayan river systems: the **Indus**, the **Ganga**, and the **Brahmaputra**, along with their numerous tributaries.
 
• **Alluvial soil** is the most widespread soil category in India, covering approximately **40 percent** of the country's total land area. It is considered the most productive and fertile soil type due to its rich mineral content.
 
• The soil consists of varying proportions of **sand**, **silt**, and **clay**. As one moves inland from the river valleys, the soil particles appear larger, while in the upper reaches of the river valleys, the soil is often coarse.
 
• Based on its age, alluvial soil in the **Northern Plains** is classified into two types: **Bhangar** (old alluvium) and **Khadar** (new alluvium). **Bhangar** is found in the upland regions and contains **calcareous deposits** known as **'Kanker'**, whereas **Khadar** is found in the floodplains and is renewed annually.
 
• This soil is rich in essential nutrients such as **potash**, **phosphoric acid**, and **lime**, making it ideal for the cultivation of **sugarcane**, **paddy (rice)**, **wheat**, and various **pulse crops**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Black Soil:**

 
 
• Also known as **Regur soil** or **Black Cotton Soil**, it is primarily found in the **Deccan Trap** region (basalt region) covering **Maharashtra**, **Saurashtra**, **Malwa**, **Madhya Pradesh**, and **Chhattisgarh**.
 
• It is highly clayey, has high **moisture-retention capacity**, and is rich in nutrients like **calcium carbonate**, **magnesium**, and **potash**.
 
 
 
• **Laterite Soil:**
 
 
• Derived from the Latin word **'later'** (meaning brick), this soil develops in areas characterized by **high temperatures** and **heavy rainfall**, leading to intense leaching.
 
• It is commonly found in **Karnataka**, **Kerala**, **Tamil Nadu**, and hilly regions of **Odisha** and **Assam**. It is suitable for growing **cashew nuts** and **tea** when treated with fertilizers.
 
 
 
• **Yellow and Red Soil:**
 
 
• **Red soil** develops on **crystalline igneous rocks** in areas of **low rainfall** in the eastern and southern parts of the **Deccan Plateau**.
 
• The soil develops a **reddish color** due to the diffusion of **iron** in crystalline and metamorphic rocks; it appears **yellow** when it occurs in a **hydrated form**.
 
 
 
• **Arid Soil:**
 
 
• These soils range from red to brown in color and are generally **sandy in texture** and **saline in nature**. They are found mostly in **Western Rajasthan**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• In the **Northern Plains**, the alluvial soil is also identified through regional variations like the **Duars**, **Chos**, and **Terai**, which are characteristic piedmont plains.
 
• The **density of population** is highest in the **alluvial soil regions** because the land is highly suitable for **intensive agriculture**, providing food security for a vast majority of the Indian population.
 
• Beyond the **Northern Plains**, this soil is also found in the **eastern coastal plains**, particularly in the deltas of the **Mahanadi**, **Godavari**, **Krishna**, and **Cauvery** rivers, as well as in narrow corridors in **Gujarat** and **Rajasthan**.

questions.question: In the context of Balance of Payment, current account does record which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Grants**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Balance of Payments (BoP)** is a comprehensive record of all **economic transactions** between the residents of a country and the rest of the world during a specific period, usually a **financial year**. It consists of two main components: the **Current Account** and the **Capital Account**.
 
• The **Current Account** records the **export and import of goods and services**, as well as **unilateral transfers**. **Grants** fall under the category of unilateral transfers because they are one-way transactions that do not involve a claim for repayment. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• **Foreign Institutional Investment (FII)** refers to investments made by **foreign entities** in the **financial markets** of a country, such as **stocks** and **bonds**. These represent changes in the **ownership of financial assets** and are recorded in the **Capital Account**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** involves a long-term investment by a **foreign company** or individual into the **productive capacity** of another country, often involving **management control**. Since it involves **capital flows** that affect the **assets and liabilities** of a country, it is a part of the **Capital Account**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **External Borrowings**, including **External Commercial Borrowings (ECB)** and **loans** from **international organizations** like the **IMF** or **World Bank**, create a **liability** for the country. Consequently, these transactions are recorded in the **Capital Account** rather than the current account. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Components of the Current Account:**

 
 
• **Visible Trade:** This includes the **export and import of physical goods** (merchandise). The difference between these is known as the **Balance of Trade (BoT)**.
 
• **Invisible Trade:** This involves **services** like **banking**, **insurance**, **shipping**, and **tourism**. It also includes **income** from **profits**, **interest**, and **dividends** earned on overseas assets.
 
• **Unilateral Transfers:** These are **transfer payments** received by or sent from a country without any corresponding exchange of goods or services. Examples include **remittances** from **migrant workers**, **gifts**, and **foreign grants**.
 
 
 
• **Components of the Capital Account:**
 
 
• **Investments:** This covers **Direct Investment (FDI)** and **Portfolio Investment (FII/FPI)**.
 
• **External Assistance:** This includes **concessional loans** provided by **foreign governments** or **multilateral agencies**.
 
• **Banking Capital:** This refers to **foreign currency assets** held by **commercial banks** and **Non-Resident Indian (NRI) deposits**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Deficit and Surplus:** A **Current Account Deficit (CAD)** occurs when the total **value of imports** of goods, services, and transfers **exceeds** the total **value of exports**. Conversely, a **surplus** occurs when exports exceed imports.
 
• **Remittances:** India is historically one of the **largest recipients of remittances** in the world, which significantly bolsters its **Current Account**. These are classified as **private transfers**.
 
• **Autonomous vs. Accommodating Items:** **Autonomous items** are those transactions undertaken for **economic motives** (like profit), while **accommodating items** are transactions (like **official reserve changes**) carried out by the **Central Bank** (e.g., **RBI** in India) to bridge the **BoP gap**.
 
• **Accounting Principle:** The **BoP** follows a **double-entry bookkeeping system**. In an accounting sense, the **BoP always balances** (Sum of Current Account, Capital Account, and Errors and Omissions equals zero).

questions.question: Who is the author of the book 'Joseph Anton: A Memoir'?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The book titled **'Joseph Anton: A Memoir'** is an autobiographical work written by the world-renowned novelist **Salman Rushdie**, published in **September 2012**.
 
• The memoir chronicles **Rushdie's** life during the decade he spent in hiding following the **fatwa** (a religious decree calling for his death) issued by **Ayatollah Khomeini**, the Supreme Leader of **Iran**, on **February 14, 1989**.
 
• The fatwa was a response to the publication of his **1988** novel, **'The Satanic Verses'**, which was deemed blasphemous by some members of the Muslim community.
 
• The title **'Joseph Anton'** refers to the pseudonym **Rushdie** adopted for his security and protection while living under the surveillance of the **British** police's **Specialist Protection Command**.
 
• He chose the name by combining the first names of two of his favorite literary figures: **Joseph Conrad** and **Anton Chekhov**.
 
• A unique feature of this memoir is that it is written in the **third person**, as **Rushdie** refers to himself as "he" or "Joseph Anton" throughout the narrative to reflect the sense of detachment he felt from his own life during those years. ***Hence, the correct answer is Salman Rushdie.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• His other notable works include **'Shame'** (**1983**), **'The Moor’s Last Sigh'** (**1995**), and **'Victory City'** (**2023**).

• The city is renowned for its **Indo-Saracenic** style of architecture, which was a revivalist style used by **British** architects in the late **19th century**. It combines **Gothic**, **Islamic**, and **Hindu** architectural elements.

• **Urban Planning:** The **British** designed **tree-lined avenues** and "garden houses" in areas like **Nungambakkam**, **Adyar**, and **Egmore**. These wide roads and green canopies remain a distinct part of the city's old-world charm.
 
• **Religious Heritage:** **San Thome Basilica** is an important landmark built over the tomb of **St. Thomas**. While originally **Portuguese**, it was rebuilt by the **British** in **1893** in a grand **Neo-Gothic** style with tall spires.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

questions.question: How does the Choice-Based Credit System (CBCS) differ from the traditional higher education system?

options.text: It allows students to pick courses based on their career goals.
It requires students to follow a fixed curriculum with no flexibility.
It limits students to a single discipline and discourages skill development.
It focuses solely on memorization and theoretical knowledge.

questions.solution:

• The passage explicitly states that CBCS **"empowers students with the autonomy to shape their academic journey according to their interests and aspirations."**

• This is **incorrect**. This description applies to the **traditional education structures** mentioned in the text, which CBCS is designed to replace with a more "dynamic" and flexible framework.
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: It limits students to a single discipline and discourages skill development.***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The text highlights that CBCS specifically includes **"interdisciplinary and skill-based"** courses alongside core subjects.
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: It focuses solely on memorization and theoretical knowledge.***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. By including **"skill-based"** courses and focusing on "holistic development," the system moves away from a purely theoretical or rote-learning approach.
